title: Build a Stage 6 Computing Showcase
overview: Bring together everything from Stage 6 Computing into one showcase: a working program, the data behind it, a clear explanation of how it runs, and the safety rules you followed while making it.

project.drivingQuestion: How can I use the computing I learned in Stage 6 to build something that solves a real problem for someone in my community — and explain exactly how it works?
project.finalProduct: A working program or digital product, the plan and algorithm behind it, a test-and-debug log, a data display, and a spoken or written explanation of your design decisions.

stages.title: 1. Plan and decompose
stages.prompt: Choose a real problem. Using the ideas from Units 1, 2, break it into smaller parts and write the algorithm before you write any code.
stages.evidence: A decomposed problem and a written algorithm or flowchart

stages.title: 2. Build it
stages.prompt: Build your program or product using the tools from Units 3, 4. Build the smallest working version first, then add one feature at a time.
stages.evidence: A working program or digital product

stages.title: 3. Test, debug and improve
stages.prompt: Test your work against your success criteria. Keep a log of every bug: what you saw, what caused it, and how you fixed it.
stages.evidence: A test-and-debug log with at least three entries

stages.title: 4. Share it safely
stages.prompt: Present your showcase. Explain three design decisions, show your data, and say which online-safety rules from Units 1, 2, 3, 4 you followed and why.
stages.evidence: A spoken, written or recorded explanation covering design, data and safety

evidenceChecklist: A decomposed problem with a written algorithm or flowchart
A working program or digital product
A test-and-debug log with at least three fixed bugs
Success criteria, each one ticked off with evidence
An explanation of your design decisions and the safety rules you followed

rubric.secure: The problem is decomposed, the algorithm is precise, and the pattern behind it is named.
The program runs, meets its criteria, and every bug found is logged with its cause and fix.
Data is collected accurately, organised sensibly and displayed so it answers a question.
Personal information is protected, sources are credited, and safety choices are explained.

questions.question: In a flowchart, which shape is used for a decision?
options: oval
rectangle
diamond
arrow
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: 1 (c) diamond. The diamond asks a Yes/No question and chooses a path. The oval is for Start/End.

questions.question: A variable is best described as:
options: a fixed number
a named box that stores a value that can change
a type of loop
a sound
questions.answer: a named box that stores a value that can change
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: 6 (b) a named box that stores a value that can change. That is exactly what a variable is.

questions.question: What does 'random' mean in programming?
options: always the same
an outcome you cannot predict
very fast
broken
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: 11 (b) an outcome you cannot predict. Like rolling a dice — you cannot know the result in advance.

questions.question: What does “attribute” mean in computing?
options: The data found in one field of one record in a database.
A function, written =AVERAGE(), that finds the mean of the selected cells.
Data that can be grouped into categories, such as favourite colour.
One box in a spreadsheet grid, where a row and a column meet.
questions.answer: The data found in one field of one record in a database.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Attribute means the data found in one field of one record in a database..

questions.question: What does “cell reference” mean in computing?
options: A cell's address, made of its column letter and row number, such as B3.
A picture of data, such as a column chart or pie chart, that makes patterns easy to see.
To work together with others on the same task.
Numerical data that can take any value, including decimals, such as temperature.
questions.answer: A cell's address, made of its column letter and row number, such as B3.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Cell means one box in a spreadsheet grid, where a row and a column meet.

questions.question: Which computing word matches this meaning: An organised set of data, made up of records and fields.?
options: database
data logger
data type
discrete data
questions.hint: Use the Unit 2 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Criteria means the requirements or conditions you search for to find matching data.

questions.question: What does “server” mean in computing?
options: A computer that provides services such as storage and programs to other computers in a network.
A large group of connected servers working together in one place.
A private network inside one organisation, only for its members — like a school's own network.
Playing a video or sound file over an internet connection instead of downloading it first.
questions.answer: A computer that provides services such as storage and programs to other computers in a network.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Server means a computer that provides services such as storage and programs to other computers in a network.

questions.question: What does “wireless” mean in computing?
options: Sending data without wires or cables, using radio waves instead.
A type of energy used to carry data through the air over long distances.
A way to connect devices to the internet using radio waves instead of wires, through a router.
A huge network of communication towers that mobile phones connect to.
questions.answer: Sending data without wires or cables, using radio waves instead.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Wireless means sending data without wires or cables, using radio waves instead.

questions.question: Which computing word matches this meaning: A small parcel of data — part of a file that travels through a network.?
options: packet
bandwidth
network overload
malware
questions.hint: Use the Unit 3 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Packet means a small parcel of data — part of a file that travels through a network.

questions.question: What does “hardware” mean in computing?
options: The physical parts of a computer that you can touch, such as the keyboard, screen and processor.
The programs and code that run on a computer. You cannot touch software.
An individual part of something larger, for example one part of a computer.
The range of tasks that a device or piece of software can do.
questions.answer: The physical parts of a computer that you can touch, such as the keyboard, screen and processor.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Hardware means the physical parts of a computer that you can touch, such as the keyboard, screen and processor.

questions.question: What does “aesthetics” mean in computing?
options: How something looks or appears to people.
How long something lasts, or its ability to keep being useful.
Suitable for the job we want to use it for.
Software that is free of charge — you do not pay to use it.
questions.answer: How something looks or appears to people.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Aesthetics means how something looks or appears to people.

questions.question: Which computing word matches this meaning: A way of writing commands to create a program a computer can understand.?
options: programming language
programming environment
block-based language
text-based language
questions.hint: Use the Unit 4 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Programming language means a way of writing commands to create a program a computer can understand.
